To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the MAPK/ERKS, SAPK/JNKS and p38 kinomes are differentially expressed following excitotoxic insult, and that the MAPKs and their specific transcriptional factor targets CREB, ATF-2 and Elk-1 are associated with cell survival, whereas the SAPKs and p38s are associated with cell death.
the activation of JNK/P38/c-Jun and MAPK/CREB/P/Elk-1/ATF-2 signalling cascades are associated with cell death and cell-survival respectively, following QA-induced excitotoxic insult.
the activation of MAPKs, JNKs, p38s, CREB, Elk1, and ATF2 is involved in the cell death or cell rescue following excitotoxic insult.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of cell death and cell protection triggered by excitotoxic insults.
the mechanisms involved in cell damage and cell survival following neurotoxic insults.
the molecular mechanisms underlying excitotoxicity, which are considered a major cell-death inductor in neuro-degeneration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
JNK/P38 activation is associated with cell death, whereas MAPK/ERk activation is associated with survival.

JNK/P38/c-Jun pathway is activated and involved in cell death, whereas MAPK/CREB/Elk-1/ATF-2 pathway, but not c-Myc, is activated and involved cell survival following QA-induced excitotoxicity in rats.
MAPK/ERKS and SAPK/JNKs are activated in response to QA excitotoxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MAPK/ERKS and p38 are associated with cell survival, whereas JNK and c-Jun are associated with cell death.
MAPKs are involved in cell survival, whereas JNKs and p38s are involved in excitotoxicity-induced cell death.
JNK/P38/c-Jun are pro-apoptotic, whereas MAPK/CREB/Elk-1/ATF-2 are pro-survival.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MAPK/ERKS and SAPK/JNKs are activated in the same neurons in response to excitotoxic insult, but they are activated at different times and they have opposite functions.
MAPK/ERKS, SAPK/JUNs and p38 kinas are differentially expressed in neurons and glia in response to excitotoxicity.
excitotoxicity is a complex phenomenon involving a number of signalling pathways, which are not always associated with caspases activation and apoptosis.
